Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

projr (development version)

  • Breaking: projr_restore_repo() and projr_restore_repo_wd() take remote (a title, or <type>:<title>), as projr_source() does, in place of pos, type, title and destination.

projr 0.9.0

  • Fetch raw inputs before a build runs. Register a remote under remotes and list it under build.source. Before any hook or script, the build checks the remote, stops if you have changed files locally since the last fetch, and then installs verified files. Pin a build with version: "1.2.3", or follow the latest build within a major or minor version with "1" or "1.2". Folders that already hold files are left alone by default, so offline builds keep working.

  • projr_source() fetches inputs outside a build. It uses build.source, or finds the registered remote that has published each directory, and asks whether to keep or replace files you have changed. projr_restore(), projr_source() and projr_get_github()/projr_get_local() now share the same verified download code.

  • Choose where a production build publishes with build.dest, as a name (dest: archive), a list, or a mapping with per-archive settings. Name a remote as github:archive when the same title is used for a GitHub and a local archive.

  • Breaking: archives can no longer be defined inline under build.github or build.local. Move each one to remotes.github.<title> or remotes.local.<title> and list it under build.dest. The error message says what to change. directories.<label>.source and a remote’s source: field are also removed; use build.source instead.

  • Breaking: projr_content_update() is deprecated in favour of projr_source(). Its destination argument now errors, and clear = FALSE stops when local files differ instead of overwriting them.

  • Run named pipelines. Define ordered scripts and hooks under pipelines and select them with build.pipeline or dev.pipeline, or for one build with projr_build_patch(pipeline = "sensitivity"). Select several pipelines or a glob such as model-*. Inline scripts and hooks run before or after the pipeline depending on where you place them relative to pipeline. pipeline = FALSE runs only the inline scripts.

  • Choose profiles in configuration. A profile key in _projr.yml or _projr-local.yml selects projr profiles, or projr and Quarto profiles separately. The build’s profile argument and the PROJR_PROFILE and QUARTO_PROFILE environment variables still take precedence.

  • Configuration files in .projr/config/ can use short names such as analysis.yml, default.yml and local.yml.

  • A one-off archive_github = TRUE or archive_local = TRUE build records the archive under remotes, so later restores know where it went.

  • build.restrictions.not_behind_remote lists remote names, using github:reports when a title is ambiguous.

projr 0.8.0

  • Production builds check the versions already published to their archives before rendering. By default they stop if the checkout is behind an archive or the proposed version already exists there. Set build.restrictions.rule to target to publish a newer version from an older checkout.

  • Builds that mix document types can pass different options to each build engine through args_engine. For example, use list(quarto_project = list(profile = "print"), rmd = list(quiet = TRUE)) to build a Quarto project with its print profile and render a standalone R Markdown document quietly. A single engine still accepts a flat list.

projr 0.7.0

  • projr_reproduce() runs a completed build in a fresh clone and shows which output files matched, changed, were missing or were added.
  • Download reports or inputs from a completed build with projr_get_github(), or copy them from a local analysis with projr_get_local(). Choose the labels and version you need. projr verifies the files before copying them into the folder you choose.
  • Installing projr now brings in httr, which it uses to download and upload GitHub release files. An older project pinned to projr 0.6.1 can add the missing package with renv::install("httr").
  • projr_restore() can recover missing files for an older build from a later upload when the release records an identical directory snapshot. It tries the requested version and earlier matches first and verifies every file.
  • Name archives under remotes in _projr.yml. Select them under build when you want to publish. You can keep an archive available to readers after you stop uploading new builds to it.

projr 0.6.1

  • Development builds leave VERSION and the package version in DESCRIPTION alone, including after a failed render. You can run a development build before creating either file. A dev build run inside a production README also keeps the outer build’s archive at its production version.
  • Use - exclude: scratch.R in a build.scripts or dev.scripts list to skip a file or glob. With only exclusions, projr discovers the usual scripts and documents and skips the matches. Quoted "!scratch.R" also works.
  • Manual rules in .gitignore and .Rbuildignore survive a refresh. Initialization keeps the original ignore file outside the managed section and adds editable rules for .vdoc.*, .DS_Store and Thumbs.db.
  • Package datasets use the standard data/ folder without a YAML entry. A production build collects staged datasets into the package and preserves other datasets already there. Declaring data: {path: data} also keeps datasets available to Git and R source packages by default.
  • Refreshing the managed ignore block removes its old directory heading and keeps figures linked from the root README.md visible to Git.
  • Production builds check the packages needed for a root README.Rmd before running analysis scripts.
  • If adding a package DESCRIPTION makes renv select an empty library, builds can still use the packages already installed in this checkout’s analysis library. Quarto and its pre-build checks use the same project library.
  • The tracked build history is now .projr/BUILDLOG.md. Older checkouts keep their entries when the log moves. CHANGELOG.md stays at the root.
  • When a file has stayed the same since its first build, projr_manifest_file_last_change() now reports the version where it first appeared.

projr 0.6.0

Changes for existing projects

  • The first interactive build of a checkout asks once for permission to run its scripts and hooks, write configured files, and perform the requested Git or archive operations. For an unattended build, pass the checkout root as project. From that root, use projr_build(project = ".", archive_github = TRUE) to publish.
  • Use build.scripts and dev.scripts to select scripts in project YAML. In projr_build_dev(), replace file = with scripts =. An empty selection skips scripts and rendering.
  • Declare a path under directories for each label your project uses. Configured paths resolve from the project root, including when code runs in a subdirectory. A first build creates a starter _projr.yml if needed. It uses _raw_data/ for inputs and _output/ for results.
  • Project metadata now lives under .projr/. You can keep the base _projr.yml at the project root or put it in .projr/config/ alongside named profiles. Directory histories live in .projr/manifests/, and detailed build logs live in .projr/logs/.
  • A production build imports history from an existing root manifest.csv. Each directory now has its own human-readable version index and file lists. Repeated directory contents reuse the earliest matching snapshot.

Building and restoring an analysis

  • Use projr_build(archive_github = TRUE) to publish versioned inputs and outputs to a GitHub release. In a fresh copy of the project, check out the desired build and call projr_restore() to recover its raw inputs. Restore verifies file paths and hashes before replacing local files.
  • Combine R scripts, standalone documents and one Quarto or Bookdown project in a single build. An explicit selection renders the project at its last selected document. With automatic selection, the project renders first, followed by top-level R scripts in alphabetical order.
  • Native hashing streams file contents and defaults to one worker. Set settings.hashing.cores to increase parallelism or select settings.hashing.approach: legacy to use the previous hashing method. Both approaches produce compatible file hashes.
  • A receiving output directory can include other declared directories. A destination name can use @version, @branch or @uuid to separate archived builds.
  • Production builds detect an existing renv project and record package versions before and after rendering. Set build.renv to true to start a lockfile or false to skip snapshots.
  • Build progress shows the steps projr actually attempts. When a render or Git push fails, the detailed build log records where it stopped.

projr 0.0.8.9002

  • Builds began checking for missing optional packages before rendering and reporting the installation commands for them.
  • GitHub Releases gained diagnostic messages for uploads, downloads and retries.
